title: Server-side request and fetch (SSRF)
status: AUTHORED. Small domain, high impact, and the one where the honest answer is often 'closed'.

atom_notes.A02: the fetcher makes a request with the server's authority, which is the whole primitive
atom_notes.A01: the URL is data that an HTTP client interprets, and clients differ in what they accept
atom_notes.A07: internal services are reachable resources that were never meant to be addressable
atom_notes.A08: the response may come back to you, or may only be observable as a callback or a timing difference

required_cells.why: finding the fetch primitive in real traffic beats guessing at parameters
escalation to an internal service is the impact
a blind SSRF needs an out of band oracle or it is not proven
metadata to credential is the highest value path and needs its own proof

tree.q: Can you see the response, or only its effect?
tree.why: Visible response means a full read primitive and possibly protocol smuggling. Blind means you need an out of band oracle, and without one you have nothing.

branches.action: enumerate internal services and try protocol smuggling through gopher where the client allows it
out of band listener first. the callback is the finding, and its metadata is the impact
read the capture. server side fetches show up as outbound requests from the app, not from you
